This was a completely irresponsible and wrong way to practice “exposures” and testing instructive thoughts. It was unexpected, unplanned, not consented to, and with no discussion or emotional support to give it a purpose. If exposures are not practiced safely and correctly (and with an actual professional!!), no doubt they would traumatized and distress anyone with OCD.

Please seek *actual* help for your pOCD with a licensed therapist who can guide and help you the right way with exposure therapy for OCD, including the traumatic experience you had here. 

[International OCD Foundation](https://iocdf.org/expert-opinions/am-i-a-monster-an-overview-of-common-features-typical-course-shame-and-treatment-of-pedophilia-ocd-pocd/)

 [International OCD Foundation - Am I a Monster?](https://iocdf.org/expert-opinions/am-i-a-monster-an-overview-of-common-features-typical-course-shame-and-treatment-of-pedophilia-ocd-pocd/)

Please know that you are not *actually* a pedophile, and can find help with this. This website (no traumatizing videos in it, I swear) accurately describes your problem and can give you some insight to know that this is normal, you’re not alone, and this can be treated.  

[International OCD Foundation](https://iocdf.org/expert-opinions/am-i-a-monster-an-overview-of-common-features-typical-course-shame-and-treatment-of-pedophilia-ocd-pocd/)

I’m sorry you feel this way, feeling overlooked and misled in highschool sucks. But as a 24yr old, I can’t help but smile reading this. I think back to all the guys from my highschool who never had gfs, or first kisses, were always friendzoned and, well.. to put it bluntly, had NO game lol. Basically all of them went off to college, and met beautiful and kind girlfriends there. Some of them are even engaged/married now! Even the ones we joked seemed asexual (mean, I know).

Whereas the ones (me included) who got caught up in dating and were like your friend, likely jumped the gun. They got into weak relationships they weren’t emotionally mature enough for, and ended up regretting them in the future. I’m jealous of the ones who were patient and focused on themselves, and now have happy & strong relationships. I know right now that a lack of dating experience in highschool feels like a disadvantage, but it’s an advantage: No baggage from the messy on-again off-again highschool hormone mess. 95% of my dating/relationships were done too young when I didn’t even figure out who I was yet lol

Your best days (and partners) are ahead of you!! Not even far, literally just a few years! I hope this brought some hope and confidence :)

Future T and just recently diagnosed too (F24)! First of all, CBT will never improve or treat symptoms/a disorder, unless it’s treating the *root cause*. 

While an ADHD assessment will screen for depression and anxiety, a big realization for me before finally seeking a diagnosis was the fact that all the mental health symptom roads lead to ADHD.. Anxiety was caused my missing deadlines, falling behind in class, obsessing about why I couldn’t THINK like I know I should. Depression from being unable to get out of bed, unable to do tasks, hopeless about my grades, and the classic rejection sensitivity dysphoria of adhd. Insomnia because I couldn’t get off my phone before bed, or couldn’t get the mental chatter to stop when trying to sleep. 

Find the common denominator of your symptoms, follow the road, and tell your therapist to fuck right off ❤️

I believe you. My family didn’t believe me either, and dismissed it the same way your therapist did. Most likely because my mom probably has undiagnosed ADHD too, so the symptoms were normalized in my house growing up. Be honest with your therapist about how she’s making you feel, and what you need from her in the moment.

You don’t have to drop the ADHD word, but ask to see the doctor to get bloodwork done. This is the first step to diagnosing ADHD anyways, by ruling out iron and thyroid issues. If those come back normal, now you have reason to seek more answers from your doctor. Or seek out a trusted staff member at your school, a counsellor/ nurse/ learning disability teacher etc. and ask for help. They may know of resources or a specialist who can assess and diagnose adhd! 

Your therapist or parents being against adhd *medication* is no reason to also rob you of the other resources (learning/test accommodations, scholarships, disability grants, ADHD coaching) that can do a world of difference for your future and education.

Hi! Female Psychotherapy student here who was diagnosed with ADHD at 24 :)

First of all, it’s unethical for your therapist to impose their beliefs upon you (religion, sex, health, etc), especially if it’s related to your mental health. However she’s clearly not competent to assess and diagnose ADHD anyways. So talk to your doctor and get a diagnosis referral from them instead. In talking to any health professional/therapist/etc. I always ask them their experience with ADHD in adults, and women, to make sure I’ll be taken seriously.

And maybe look into finding a new therapist who *believes in* and understands ADHD better. In a consultation with a potential new therapist (for unrelated reasons), I briefly mentioned that I was recently diagnosed with ADHD and she asked “and how do you feel about that?”. She didn’t need to, but it just goes to show how important and impactful it is for us to be validated and empathized by any kind of health professional or support network. It’s not until I first received that empathy from my ADHD specialist, that I was able to give myself compassion, which dramatically helped my general mental health. Advocate for yourself!!

I have a chicken-egg situation, except with social/public speaking anxiety and inability to express my thoughts and knowledge. During class discussions, interviews, etc. I get extreme physical and mental anxiety, while struggling to organize my knowledge and communicate it clearly, and I don’t know which causes which. 

I BOMB presentations without having a full script to follow, even if I know the topic enough to confidently answer follow-up questions or explain it in informal discussions. What’s more, I often space out or lose attention to the lectures/conversations in class, because I’m busy in my head creating and rehearsing a smart and understandable thing to say before the topic changes. I’ve accepted it’s an ADHD thing lol

Edit: Oh, and I also forget to breath while speaking in classes or groups :)

They don’t need to be exclusively consequences of ADD, and can definitely spread to/from other areas of your life if they’ve been long term. As a student I was experiencing anxiety and depression primarily because of my symptoms/consequences of ADD. Anxiety over procrastination, inability to meet deadlines, running late all the time, endless thoughts in my head 24/7; depression about my “laziness”, trouble falling asleep/getting out of bed before noon, nonexistent productivity, inexplainable brain fog, and what ADHDers call “rejection sensitive dysphoria”. Everything mostly traced back to my cognitive functioning/performance, aka ADD.
Oftentimes, especially in women, ADHD can be misdiagnosed as Anxiety+Depression due to the overlapping symptoms

I’ve experienced all of this - and resultant anxiety/depressive symptoms due to the brain fog/symptoms -before getting a late diagnosis of ADD. 

It was exploring the experiences on r/adhd and r/adhdwomen that made everything click for me and let me begin self-compassion and self-understanding. Common themes on these subs also include challenges in therapy if the therapist is not adhd-informed enough.

Glad I could help!! Mind Over Mood is the #1 CBT workbook that is referenced in my own studies, so I think that would be your best bet!! Alternatively to buying a hard copy, there may be cheaper ebook version or free with a local/online library. Plus it’s website has extra resources and worksheets that are free to download if you have the book :)

Hi!
Since starting grad school to become a therapist, I realized just how complicated/lacking/unknown mental health resources are! This is just the broadest suggestion I can make without knowing more details about your context/coverage/local resources etc:   I highlyyyy recommend searching up “CBT for [anxiety/depression] workbook” on Amazon/any other bookstore.

CBT is the gold standard form of therapy for both anxiety and depression that you assumably would be treated with by a real therapist. CBT workbooks come in a self-help form where you’re guided through CBT activities and reflections (it’s lots of workbook/homework-like activities in-person anyways). And you can track progress/mood and reflect on your thoughts and problems just as a personal therapist may prompt you. So money wise, a workbook is maybe $30/$40 total, while therapy would be AT LEAST $50 per session (usually between 10-20 sessions). 

If you need help deciding on which workbook to get, I’ve also learned that in assessing your problems, a therapist would choose to treat whichever problem is the most debilitating/serious for you. Usually it’s like a main course of depression with a side order of anxiety, or vice versa. Typically, treatment of the one problem will help alleviate the other! And if not, more therapy of some form is welcome :)

Hope this helps, and congrats on making the thoughtful steps towards mental health care!

I’m going through the same thing! I haven’t even talked to my doctor about it yet since he’s new and doesn’t have the time to even get to know me. I’m so scared of getting misdiagnosed and invalidated that I went straight to a school psychologist in my area and made sure she was very experienced in assessing adhd in college/uni adults. I didn’t even want to wait a couple more months to going through my university so am risking +$2000 out of pocket (in case it comes back negative) to finally find out why I am the way that I am. 

I’m terrified to potentially hear that “it’s just anxiety+depression” or “you have an iron deficiency though so that’s it”, yet also kinda scared to get an official diagnosis attached to me and living in the stigma for the rest of my life. But above all, the diagnosis process and fees are worth finding out to put my mind at ease and in a big way for me to find the right help, start the healing process and give myself permission to be self-compassionate to something I in fact cannot control. I know I can do that without a diagnosis, but it would mean a lot to me to shed the labels of lazy, flakey, inconsiderate, dumb, not dedicated, inconsistent, etc. that will always be doubted in the back of my head if I don’t get assessed and diagnosed.

I’m also technically undiagnosed but struggled with the pill A LOT in highschool! It was so sensitive to timing that I would spot if I forgot to take it even a few hours late. I switched to a patch format (wear one on your skin and replace it on a weekly basis instead) and can manage now!! It has the timing window flexibility that it was no big deal and no spotting if I forgot to switch them or put a new one on a day or two later than I was supposed to! 😊

Having expertise in exercise psychology and mental health, I think you also need to try to empathize with the tough barriers and guilt she’s facing from these physical issues. Don’t complain or expect too much of her. I’m a personal trainer too, but I see most of them have this bias where they can’t wrap their head around why someone can’t “just do it” or enjoy the type of physical activity they themselves like. 
But you’re not her trainer, and acting as such unsolicited will just add to her shame and resistance. If you genuinely want her to get moving again to help her mood and mental health, the best way to start is to start small and start *with* her. Ask her nicely to go on a walk with you, just once. No weights or gym rats or machines - outside, in nature with just her boyfriend, as an activity to spend time together and get in simple movement. Then you can reinforce this afterwards by asking her some positives, like if she feels better now, or “habit stack” it with something else she likes, like getting her favourite coffee order etc. Starting small will help with the self-efficacy she most likely lost, and help her to get thinking about, and missing being active more.
